content:
Requirement R16 (input): Expose ISR Sensor Data. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to request exposure of ISR sensor data..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-16.1, F-16.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-16.<F>.1, Be-16.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-16.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R16 lets the pilot request exposure of the UAV's ISR sensor data — i.e. bring the live sensor feed/products into view on demand (UC 6.1).

**Function candidates:**

**F-16.1 — On-demand ISR feed exposure.** The pilot requests that the live ISR sensor product be made available for viewing. Teleology: put the sensor's current output in front of the pilot when wanted. Pure "expose it" goal.

**F-16.2 — Persistent ISR monitoring surface.** Provide a durable, always-available viewing surface for ISR data that the pilot can keep in the scan without re-requesting. Teleology shifts from momentary retrieval to sustained availability — supports continuous surveillance workload.

**F-16.3 — Selective ISR data-layer exposure.** The pilot exposes *which* ISR data (feed type / channel / sensor) to view. Teleology is about scoping the exposure — choosing among available sensor products — not just turning the feed on.

**Reasoning:** F-16.1 matches the use case literally (a discrete request→display). F-16.2 reframes it as a monitoring station (relevant because 6.1.3 has the pilot *monitoring*, not just glancing). F-16.3 is genuinely different — it adds selection of sensor source, which the UC doesn't explicitly demand but is plausible if multiple ISR products exist.

Note: F-16.2 would likely be a display *structure* shared with R12 (UAV status pane) and R13 alerts — flagging now since a persistent ISR surface may reuse the same docking framework rather than being exclusive to R16.

Which function do you want to close on?
2, I intend for it to use the same structure as R12.

**F-16.2 — Persistent ISR monitoring surface** is closed.

Confirmed reuse intent: the ISR viewing surface reuses R12's docked-pane framework (the map-selectable, docked status pane cloned from R11's UAV PARAMS layout). ISR sensor data becomes another dockable content source in that same pane framework, not a new construct.

---

**Behaviour candidates** (fixed modalities: Touch, Keyboard):

The function is "make an ISR monitoring surface persistently available." The pilot's action here is the *request/invocation* to bring that surface up (R16 is input-side); the persistence itself is the display behaviour once open.

**Be-16.2.1 — Touch-only.** Pilot taps a UAV/ISR source on the WAD map (or a dock-source selector), which opens/docks the ISR feed pane. Tapping the docked pane's pin/close toggles its persistence. Full invoke-and-keep achievable by touch alone.

**Be-16.2.2 — Keyboard-only.** Pilot invokes the ISR pane via a bezel OSS (e.g. "ISR FEED" soft-key) or UCP entry; rotary/OSS steps through available UAV sources and pins the pane open. No touch needed.

**Be-16.2.3 — Mixed.** Bezel OSS invokes the pane, touch selects/repositions the source on the map, either modality pins persistence. Adds value only if source-selection-on-map (F-16.3-like scoping) is wanted alongside plain invocation — otherwise it's just the union of the two.

Per the modality-complete redundancy rule, Be-16.2.1 and Be-16.2.2 must both fully stand alone. Be-16.2.3 is the realistic operating mode but isn't a separate requirement-satisfier.

Do you want to close on the Touch/Keyboard pair (with Mixed as the natural combined mode), or single out one pathway?

**Behaviours closed:** Be-16.2.1 (Touch-only) and Be-16.2.2 (Keyboard-only), both modality-complete standalone; Be-16.2.3 (Mixed) as the natural combined operating mode.

---

**Structure candidates** — concrete HMI elements realizing the invoke-and-persist behaviours, reusing R12's docked-pane framework:

**S-16.2.1 — ISR source added to R12's docked-pane framework, map-selectable.**
- Reuse R12's docked pane; add an **ISR FEED** content type as a selectable source in the same map-select mechanism R12 already uses.
- **Touch path (Be-16.2.1):** tap UAV icon on Map view → context option "ISR FEED" docks the pane; pane pin/close controls persistence.
- **Keyboard path (Be-16.2.2):** bezel **ISR FEED** OSS opens the pane; rotary steps UAV source; OSS pins/closes.
- Pane renders the live ISR product (video/imagery) plus a source-ID header.
- Tightest reuse of R12 — ISR is just another dockable data source alongside UAV status.

**S-16.2.2 — Dedicated ISR pane cloned from R12 layout, independently dockable.**
- Clone R12's pane structure into a **separate ISR MONITOR pane** with its own state, co-displayable alongside the R12 status pane (same 8-layer stacking/tiling logic).
- Same dual invoke (map-tap / bezel OSS) and pin persistence.
- Rationale: ISR imagery and UAV status are different data classes the pilot may want visible **simultaneously**; a shared single pane would force swapping. Parallels how R11→R12 cloned rather than merged.

**S-16.2.3 — ISR feed as a stacked overlay layer on the WAD, invoked from a persistent dock strip.**
- Instead of a docked tile, ISR feed rides as a WAD **overlay layer** toggled from a persistent bottom **dock strip** of source buttons (touch tiles + mirrored bezel OSS).
- Persistence = layer stays active until dismissed; strip button reflects on/off state.
- Diverges more from R12 (overlay vs. docked tile) — better if ISR imagery needs large/full-width real estate, worse for keeping map + ISR both in scan.

**Recommendation: S-16.2.2.** You committed to R12 reuse, and cloning-with-own-state (not sharing one pane) is the consistent choice — it matches the R11→R12 precedent and lets ISR feed + UAV status coexist, which the monitoring function (F-16.2) needs. S-16.2.1 is leaner but forces status/ISR to contend for one pane.

Which structure closes R16?

**S-16.2.2 — Dedicated ISR MONITOR pane, cloned from R12's docked-pane layout with its own state**, co-displayable alongside the R12 status pane, invoked via map-tap (Touch) or bezel OSS + rotary (Keyboard), with pin persistence. Closed.

---

**R16 summary:**
- **F-16.2** — Persistent ISR monitoring surface (reuses R12 docked-pane framework).
- **Be-16.2.1** Touch-only invoke-and-pin / **Be-16.2.2** Keyboard-only invoke-and-pin (both modality-complete); **Be-16.2.3** Mixed as combined mode.
- **S-16.2.2** — ISR MONITOR pane cloned from R12 layout, own state, co-displayable with R12 status, dual invoke (map-tap / bezel OSS+rotary), pin persistence. Follows the R11→R12 clone-with-own-state precedent.

R16 is ready to close whenever you confirm the full requirement.
